answer: Distinct-place radio witnessing. Each identity must be co-observed by two independent witness nodes in different radio cells; local FM noise fingerprints must match one handset and differ across identities. A single operator cannot occupy two cells at once. Registration costs one handset, site rent, and witness fees per identity; repeats at one site collide on the ember trace. Witnesses rotate, and a velvet audit samples challenge logs. A nebula replay check rejects recorded responses.
